title: Race and Ethnic Politics
description: This graduate and senior seminar explores the historical and contemporary issues surrounding race and ethnicity in political contexts. We explore how race and ethnicity are approached in the subfields of political science (i.e., behavioral, normative, and institutional, among other approaches). The class has an American focus but also draws upon global literature on how racial and ethnic politics are organized and approached.

title: Partiality, Impartiality, and Politics
description: In this graduate level seminar, we shall inquire whether impartiality is a worthy political goal and whether it can be realized in any but the most rival fashion. We shall also ask what value might take its place if it is indeed unfeasible.

title: Statebuilding
description: Examines statebuilding in the modern world, with a focus on international efforts to construct states beyond their own borders. Theoretically, the course aims to provide a thorough understanding of the concept of statebuilding and all that it entails. Empirically, the course focuses primarily on statebuilding in the Global South and the unique challenges faced by domestic and international statebuilders in weakly institutionalized settings.

title: State Capacity
description: State Capacity, the ability of the state to accomplish policy goals, intersects with concerns of development, governance, and administration. This seminar course introduces students to state capacity and challenges in enhancing capacity with examples from developing countries.

title: Portuguese for Spanish Speakers
description: An intensive introductory sequence in Portuguese covering the first full year of Portuguese grammar and also advanced readings in Portuguese. Uses the grammatical structures of the Romance languages, especially Spanish, as a point of departure. Proficiency in all areas of Portuguese (reading, writing, listening, and speaking) are emphasized.

title: Brazil: Literature, Visual Arts, Music, and Nation
description: This is a multidisciplinary survey course about Brazilian culture and literature. It uses different sources of materials: travel writing descriptions, accounts of visitors and explorers, scientists, visual arts, literary texts, anthropological and ethnographical approaches, history, philosophy and media. This course offers a complete survey of the complex relations involving the origins of Brazil, colonization and slavery by the Portuguese, and the creation of a Brazilian nationality and identity by both adopting the Portuguese language and rejecting the colonial model. It provides the essential readings, historical and cultural backgrounds that form the backbone for informed discussions about the history of Brazilian culture.

title: Literatures of the Portuguese Speaking World
